identity.title: The Radial Distribution of Dust Particles in the HL Tau Disk from ALMA and VLA Observations

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here, we present an analysis of high quality ALMA and VLA images of the HL Tau protoplanetary disk, covering a wide range of wavelengths, from 0.8 mm to 1 cm

evidence.quote: equivalent to a physical size of 7.35 au at the distance of 147 pc (Galli et al. 2018)

question.value: What are the radial profiles of dust temperature, dust surface density and maximum grain size in the HL Tau disk when scattering is included and no optical depth is assumed?

evidence.quote: This procedure allows us to obtain the dust temperature, the dust surface density and the maximum particle size at each radius.

method.value: Download ALMA B7/B6 images, calibrate B4 and VLA data, subtract free-free jet in uv plane, convolve all to 50 mas

evidence.quote: convolving all images to a circular beam with a size of 50 m.a.s., equivalent to a physical size of 7.35 au

key_parameters.value: Ka and Q combined into 8.0 mm image; K band excluded

evidence.quote: We do not use the K band data for the analysis of the dust emission since the jet emission is likely to be affecting a larger part of the disk center at this band

method.value: MFS clean (nterms=2) of combined K, Ka, Q uniform-weighted image to model jet; subtract model components from uv data

evidence.quote: we subtracted the model components obtained from the MFS cleaning process to the uv data of the three VLA bands.

key_parameters.value: 175 uJy at 32.5 GHz, spectral index 0.7, size 22 mas

evidence.quote: an elongated source at 32.5 GHz with a flux density of $\sim$175 $\mu$Jy, a spectral index of $\sim$0.7

method.value: Average intensity in elliptical rings 10 mas wide using inclination and PA; convert to brightness temperature with full Planck law; compute spectral indices

evidence.quote: averaging emission in elliptical rings with a width of 10 m.a.s.
$\Delta \rm{I}_\nu = \rm{rms}_\nu / ( \Omega_{\rm ring} / \Omega_{\rm beam} )^{0.5}$

method.value: Fit each radius to I_nu with absorption+scattering slab solution for T_dust, tau_0, beta_chi; iterate a_max until converged; derive Sigma_dust=tau_0/chi_0

evidence.quote: We repeat this until $a_{\rm max}$ converges (i.e., differences are lower than 5%) which typically occurs in 2 or 3 iterations
we consider a reference frequency $\nu_0$=230 GHz, which corresponds to a wavelength of 1.3 mm

assumptions.value: p=3.5, a_min=0.05 um, compact spherical grains; silicates/organics/ice 26/31/43%; vertically isothermal slab, isotropic scattering with effective sigma

evidence.quote: with relative abundances of 26%, 31%, and 43% respectively (Pollack et al. 1994)

evidence.loc: 3 Methods: Estimating Particle Sizes from Dust Opacity
evidence.quote: it is assumed to be 0.05 $\mu$m

fitting.value: Non-linear least squares; errors from 1000 Monte Carlo realizations with normal noise; mean and std dev

evidence.quote: the nominal value of a parameter is defined as the mean and the error as the standard deviation of the 1000 fits.

validation.value: Model compared to observed brightness temperatures and to independent 3.0 mm ALMA image convolved to ~80 mas

evidence.quote: We convolved the prediction of our model at 3.0 mm to the angular resolution of this image, and compare the radial profiles of the brightness temperature.

method.value: Repeat fit 1000 times varying each profile by flux uncertainties; report 16th–84th percentiles

evidence.quote: The lower limit is defined by the percentile 16 and the upper limit as the percentile 84 of our 1000 fits.
(parameter nterms=2 in the CASA task *clean*)
we use the function *curvefit*[^4] in *python*

findings_qualitative.value: Dark rings have low dust density and small particles; inner features D13, B21, D33 coincide with snow lines, while D67-D77 is consistent with planet-disk interaction

evidence.quote: Dark rings are always associated with low dust density and small particles.

claims.hypothesis: Have particles in HL Tau grown to mm sizes when scattering is included?
claims.experiment: Radial SED fit of 0.9–8 mm images with absorption+scattering model
claims.result: a_max ~1.5 mm at center to ~0.5 mm outside
claims.finding: Millimeter-sized grains exist; inconsistent with ~100 um from polarization

evidence.loc: 4.1 The Global Particle Dust Distribution in HL Tau
evidence.quote: Our results imply that dust particles in the HL Tau disk have grown up to, at least, millimeter sizes.

claims.experiment: Compare dust properties and temperature-derived snow line positions with rings
claims.result: Inner rings coincide with snow lines; wide gap near 70 au has small particles and gas gap
claims.finding: Inner features likely snow-line related, outer planet-related

evidence.loc: 4.2 On the Nature of Bright and Dark Rings
evidence.quote: These results strongly support the idea that the most internal radial features are not created by planet-disk interactions

claims.result: a_max>>1 cm at R<50 au, lower dust mass and temperature

evidence.loc: 4.1 The Global Particle Dust Distribution in HL Tau
evidence.quote: repeating our analysis ignoring the scattering effects lead to very large sizes for the particles in the inner half part of the disk

why_this_method.value: Absorption-only, optically thin assumptions can overestimate sizes and underestimate mass

evidence.quote: leading to overestimation of particle sizes and to underestimation of the disk’s mass

evidence.quote: adding it to the analysis does not help, but results in larger uncertainties

referee_caveats_inferred: Single grain composition and p=3.5 fixed; a_max and p are degenerate
Isotropic scattering and vertically isothermal slab assumptions
Flux-scale errors treated as sqrt(N epochs) reduction, which is optimistic
Only 3 free parameters fit to 4 wavelengths
